config.title: Zustand for Global State

intro.title: Zustand for Global State
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that uses Zustand, a lightweight state management library, to manage a global counter. You will learn how to create a Zustand store with TypeScript to define your state and actions in a type-safe way. The core programming concept is global state management, which allows different components to share and update the same data without prop drilling. You will implement a store, use it in components, and see how Zustand simplifies state updates with its straightforward API.
intro.usecase: Zustand is commonly used in React applications to manage shared state across multiple components without prop drilling. For example, in an e-commerce dashboard, Zustand can store user authentication status, shopping cart items, and global UI themes, making them accessible from product listings, cart modals, and user menus. This pattern is also practical in data-heavy applications like analytics platforms, where filters, date ranges, or selected datasets need to be synchronized across charts, tables, and control panels. By centralizing state, developers can efficiently update and respond to changes in complex, interactive UIs.

objectives: Initialize a Zustand store with typed state and actions
Configure a Zustand store to manage global application state
Integrate the Zustand store into React components using hooks
Manipulate global state by dispatching actions from components
Bind component UI to automatically update when Zustand state changes
Construct a complete application using Zustand for cross-component state sharing
Apply Zustand patterns to replace prop drilling in a React TypeScript application

steps.title: Import React and Zustand
steps.instruction: Import React and the create function from zustand.
steps.hint: Use import statements at the top of your file. Remember to import from the correct packages.
steps.seedCode: // Import React and the create function from zustand
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary libraries for React and Zustand are imported.
successCriteria: React is imported from 'react' and create is imported from 'zustand'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and the create function from zustand.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statements. You need to import React from 'react' and create from 'zustand'.

steps.title: Define the store interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'StoreState' that describes the shape of your global store. It should have a 'count' property of type number.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and its property definitions.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a TypeScript interface that defines the structure of your global state.
successCriteria: An interface named 'StoreState' is defined with a 'count' property of type number.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your interface is named 'StoreState' and includes a 'count' property of type number.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition doesn't match the requirements. Check the name and property type.

steps.title: Create the Zustand store
steps.instruction: Create a Zustand store using the create function. Define the store with an initial state that includes a count property set to 0.
steps.hint: Use the create function imported from zustand. Pass it a function that returns an object with the initial state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Zustand store is created with an initial state containing count set to 0.
successCriteria: The store is created using create from zustand and returns an object with a count property initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the create function and defining an initial state object with count set to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store wasn't created correctly. Check that you're using create from zustand and returning an object with count: 0.

steps.title: Add state update functions to the store
steps.instruction: Inside the store you created, add two functions: one named 'increment' that increases the count by 1, and another named 'decrement' that decreases the count by 1.
steps.hint: Remember that Zustand store functions receive a 'set' parameter to update the state. Use it to modify the 'count' property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store now includes 'increment' and 'decrement' functions that update the 'count' state when called.
successCriteria: The store contains both 'increment' and 'decrement' functions that use the 'set' function to modify the 'count' property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both 'increment' and 'decrement' functions are present and properly update the 'count' state using the 'set' function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store doesn't yet have the required update functions. Remember to add both 'increment' and 'decrement' functions that modify the 'count' state.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a div wrapper element.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called App that returns JSX. The component should return a div element for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns a div element.
successCriteria: App component is defined as a function or arrow function
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named App that returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Create a functional component named App that returns a div.

steps.title: Access store state in the component
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useCounterStore hook to access the count state value.
steps.hint: Call the useCounterStore hook inside your component to get the current count value from the store.
steps.analogousExample:
// Accessing state from a store
const count = useCounterStore((state) => state.count);
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have access to the current count value from the Zustand store.
successCriteria: The useCounterStore hook is called inside the App component to access the count state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useCounterStore inside the App component to get the count value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The count state hasn't been accessed from the store yet. Use the useCounterStore hook inside the App component.

steps.title: Access store functions in the component
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, use the useCounterStore hook to access the increment and decrement functions from the store.
steps.hint: Destructure the increment and decrement functions from the store hook call, similar to how you accessed the count state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Accessing functions from a Zustand store
const { increment, decrement } = useCounterStore();
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have access to both increment and decrement functions from the Zustand store.
successCriteria: The increment and decrement functions are destructured from useCounterStore() inside the App component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're accessing both increment and decrement functions from the store.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to use the useCounterStore hook to access the increment and decrement functions.

steps.title: Create the component structure
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add a <div> container with a heading that says 'Counter App'.
steps.hint: Add a <div> element as the main container, then place an <h1> element inside it with the text 'Counter App'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component returns a <div> container with an <h1> heading displaying 'Counter App'.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a <div> element with an <h1> child element that has the text 'Counter App'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have a <div> container with an <h1> heading inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure isn't quite right. Check that you have a <div> element containing an <h1> with the text 'Counter App'.

steps.title: Add buttons and wire them to store functions
steps.instruction: Add two buttons inside your component's return statement: one with the label 'Increment' and an onClick handler that calls the increment function from your store, and another with the label 'Decrement' and an onClick handler that calls the decrement function.
steps.hint: Remember to access the store functions using the same hook pattern you used for the count state. The buttons should be placed after the heading and paragraph.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two functional buttons that update the global count state when clicked.
successCriteria: Two buttons are added with labels 'Increment' and 'Decrement', each with onClick handlers that call the corresponding store functions.
